examples.input: Write landing page copy for a SaaS tool that automates expense reports. Target: finance teams at companies with 50-500 employees. They currently use spreadsheets and email. Product costs $15/user/month. Free trial available.

strategy.awareness_stage: Problem-Aware — they know expense reports are painful but may not know automation tools exist or believe they're worth the cost for their company size
strategy.primary_conversion_goal: Start free trial (no credit card required)
key_objections: Our current process works fine (it doesn't, but change is scary)
It's too expensive for our team size
Our team won't adopt another tool

hero.headline: Stop Chasing Receipts. Start Closing Books Faster.
hero.subheadline: Expense reports that file themselves. Built for finance teams who are done with spreadsheets, lost receipts, and month-end chaos.
hero.cta: Start Free Trial — No Credit Card
hero.supporting: Join 1,200+ finance teams who've eliminated manual expense tracking

problem_section.headline: You Didn't Become a Finance Professional to Chase Receipts
problem_section.copy:
Every month, the same cycle: chasing employees for overdue expense reports. Deciphering crumpled receipts. Manually entering data into spreadsheets. Reconciling corporate cards line by line. Cross-referencing policies that nobody remembers.

Your team spends 15+ hours per month on expense processing. That's 180 hours per year — a full month of work — on a process that should take minutes.

solution_section.headline: Expenses That Actually Manage Themselves
solution_section.copy:
Employees snap a photo of the receipt. Our AI reads it, categorizes it, checks it against your policy, and routes it for approval. You review exceptions, approve batches, and export to your accounting system. Done.

No spreadsheets. No email chains. No 'can you resubmit this with the right project code?'

features_benefits.benefit: Employees submit in 10 seconds instead of filling out a form. No more lost receipts or illegible photos.
Out-of-policy expenses are flagged before they reach your desk. No awkward conversations after the fact.
features_benefits.detail: Custom rules by department, amount, category, and merchant

features_benefits.benefit: Your exact approval chain, automated. Manager → VP → Finance — with automatic escalation if someone's out of office.
features_benefits.detail: Mirrors your org chart. Updates when roles change.

features_benefits.benefit: Export to QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, or Sage in one click. No manual journal entries.

testimonials.quote: We went from 20 hours/month on expense processing to 3. The ROI paid for itself in the first week.
testimonials.author: Lisa Chen, Controller

testimonials.quote: I was skeptical — our team resists new tools. But the receipt photo feature won them over. 92% adoption in the first month.
testimonials.author: David Park, VP Finance

social_proof.stats: 1,200+ finance teams | 4.8/5 on G2 | SOC 2 Type II certified

objection_handling.response: It works — but at what cost? The average finance team spends 15 hours/month on manual expense processing. That's $4,500/month in labor for a 5-person team. [Product] costs $75/month for the same team. The math is simple.
SOC 2 Type II certified. 256-bit encryption at rest and in transit. Your data never leaves US-based servers. We're more secure than the spreadsheet on your shared drive.

objection_handling.objection: What if our team won't use it?
objection_handling.response: 92% average adoption rate in the first 30 days. The secret? Employees actually prefer it — submitting an expense takes 10 seconds instead of filling out a form. We also provide onboarding support at no extra cost.

final_cta.headline: Your Month-End Close Doesn't Have to Be This Painful
final_cta.cta: Start Free Trial — No Credit Card Required
final_cta.risk_reversal: 14-day free trial. Full features. No credit card. Cancel with one click.

examples.input: Write landing page copy for a free webinar: 'How to Negotiate a $20K Raise in 2026'. Target: mid-career tech professionals (5-10 years experience) who feel underpaid but don't know how to negotiate.

strategy.awareness_stage: Problem-Aware — they know they're underpaid but feel powerless or afraid to negotiate
strategy.primary_conversion_goal: Webinar registration (free, lead gen for coaching program)
emotional_triggers: Envy of peers who negotiate successfully
Hope that there's a learnable skill

hero.headline: You're Leaving $20,000 on the Table Every Year
hero.subheadline: Join 5,000+ tech professionals who learned the exact negotiation framework that turns 'we can't do that' into 'here's your updated offer.'
hero.supporting: Live Q&A included. Can't make it? Register and get the recording.

problem_section.headline: The Raise You Deserve Won't Come by Waiting
problem_section.copy:
You're 7 years into your career. You've shipped features, mentored juniors, and carried projects. Your Glassdoor research says you're 15-25% below market.

But every time you think about asking for a raise, the same thoughts stop you:

• "What if they say no and it gets awkward?"
• "What if they think I'm being greedy?"
• "I should just wait for the next performance review."
• "I don't want to seem like I'm threatening to leave."

Here's the thing: **your manager expects you to negotiate.** They have a budget for it. The only person losing money by not asking... is you.

what_you_learn: The 3-part negotiation script that works in any company (startup to FAANG) — word for word
When to negotiate (and when NOT to — timing is 50% of the outcome)
How to research your exact market rate using 4 free data sources (not just Glassdoor)
The 'competing offer' strategy — even if you don't have a competing offer
How to negotiate beyond salary: equity, bonuses, remote work, title, PTO
